land.text: Theuderic I's share of Clovis I's kingdom at the partition of 511: 'the lands that were to become Austrasia'

predecessors.note: Austrasia is a sub-kingdom of the Frankish realm, not a state Cliopatria draws; its land sits inside the kingdom-of-the-franks shape for 511-751. The Austrasia infobox gives 481 (Clovis I's accession) as 'Established'; the text dates the separate realm to 511.

successors.note: The infobox names the Carolingian Empire as successor; the pages opened give no Carolingian state before 800, so the land returns to the Frankish kingdom.

capitals.name: Metz

region.text: Theuderic I's share, 'the lands that were to become Austrasia', with Reims as capital

ledger.note: 511: At Clovis I's death his four sons partition the Frankish kingdom and Theuderic I receives Austrasia, with his capital at Reims. 'After the death of the Frankish king Clovis I in 511, his four sons partitioned his kingdom amongst themselves, with Theuderic I receiving the lands that were to become Austrasia.' The page gives the rivers (Meuse, Moselle, Middle Rhine, Main), not a boundary.

region.text: Thuringia, the kingdom of Herminafrid; Theuderic I 'took control of the Unstrut region'

ledger.note: 532: Theuderic I's Franks overthrow the Thuringian kingdom. 'conquered by the Franks in 531-532'; Theuderic and his relatives 'defeated Herminafrid in two battles and took control of the Unstrut region'. The Francia page dates the incorporation to 532. Which Frankish king took which part of Thuringia is not stated; the whole is booked to Austrasia as the Austrasian share (reading).

region.text: the lands between the Meuse, Moselle, Middle Rhine and Main: roughly Luxembourg, eastern Belgium, Lorraine and Champagne-Ardenne, the Rhineland, Hesse and Franconia, with the southern Netherlands (Austrasia page); Thuringia

ledger.note: 555: Theudebald dies and Austrasia is absorbed by Chlothar I. 'on Theudebald's death in 555 all the lands passed to Chlothar'; the Austrasia page: 'a line of kings ruled Austrasia until 555'. Chlothar holds the whole realm by 558.

region.text: the lands between the Meuse, Moselle, Middle Rhine and Main: roughly Luxembourg, eastern Belgium, Lorraine and Champagne-Ardenne, the Rhineland, Hesse and Franconia, with the southern Netherlands (Austrasia page); Thuringia; the Auvergne

ledger.note: 561: Chlothar I's death gives Sigebert I Austrasia again. 'Sigebert I: Austrasia with its chief cities of Reims and Metz', 'The rest of Provence, the Auvergne, and eastern Aquitaine'; the Austrasia page: 'already by 561, Austrasia was ruled as a separate kingdom'. Drawn: the core, Thuringia and the Auvergne; Provence and eastern Aquitaine are not bounded by any page.

region.text: Tours and Poitiers, in Austrasian hands by 575

ledger.note: 567: Charibert I of Paris dies and his brothers share his lands; Tours and Poitiers are Austrasian by 575 ('took Tours and Poitiers from Austrasia'). The page gives no year or manner for Sigebert I's acquisition; 567 is a bridge from the page's 'The brothers agreed to share Paris and the territory around it'.

region.text: Tours, Poitiers and Saintes, taken by Chilperic I after Sigebert's murder (and 'territory in Auvergne', not bounded)

ledger.note: 575: Sigebert I is assassinated and Chilperic I of Neustria takes Tours and Poitiers from Austrasia, 'along with places in Aquitaine such as Saintes and territory in Auvergne'. The page gives no month for the gains; Guntram's troops recovered Tours and Poitiers after 584 (Chlothar II page).

region.text: Tours, ceded by Guntram

ledger.note: 587: By the Treaty of Andelot Guntram, king of Burgundy, cedes Tours to his nephew Childebert II of Austrasia, whom he adopts as heir; Gregory of Tours judged the cession significant. The page gives no further list of lands and no month.

region.text: Chilperic I's 561 share (Soissons, Arras, Cambrai, Thérouanne, Tournai, Boulogne) less Amiens, which stayed Neustrian after Dormelles

ledger.note: 599: At Dormelles Theuderic II and Theudebert II defeat Chlothar II, whose treaty 'reduced his kingdom to the regions of Beauvais, Amiens and Rouen'; the rest 'was split between' the two brothers. The page does not say which cities Austrasia received; the northern cities of Chilperic's 561 share are Austrasia's by reading (confidence 1).

ledger.note: 612: Theuderic II of Burgundy takes Austrasia from his brother Theudebert II (list: Theudebert II 595-612, Theuderic II 612-613). The Francia page: Sigebert II was 'inheritor of the kingdoms of Burgundy and Austrasia in 613'; Chlothar II then unites all three (Austrasia page, 613). The page does not describe the conquest.

region.text: the lands between the Meuse, Moselle, Middle Rhine and Main: roughly Luxembourg, eastern Belgium, Lorraine and Champagne-Ardenne, the Rhineland, Hesse and Franconia, with the southern Netherlands (Austrasia page); Thuringia

ledger.note: 623: The Austrasians ask for their own king and Chlothar II gives them his son Dagobert I, with Pepin of Landen as regent. 'Chlothar thus granted that his son Dagobert I would be their king' (Francia page). Outline reading: the core and Thuringia; Auvergne and Tours are not named.

region.text: Alsace, carved out of southern Austrasia in the last decade of Dagobert I's reign

ledger.note: 623: Alsace joins Dagobert I's Austrasia: Chlothar II 'excluded Alsace from Dagobert's Austrasia. He was soon forced to concede it.' The page gives no year for the concession; 623 is a bridge.

region.text: the lands between the Meuse, Moselle, Middle Rhine and Main: roughly Luxembourg, eastern Belgium, Lorraine and Champagne-Ardenne, the Rhineland, Hesse and Franconia, with the southern Netherlands (Austrasia page); Thuringia; Alsace

ledger.note: 629: Dagobert I inherits Neustria and Burgundy and rules the whole realm; the Francia page: in 632 he 'reunited the entire Frankish realm'. The pages do not say the Austrasian sub-kingdom lapsed; the loss is the reading that the Austrasians' demand for their own king in 633 shows it had.

region.text: the lands between the Meuse, Moselle, Middle Rhine and Main: roughly Luxembourg, eastern Belgium, Lorraine and Champagne-Ardenne, the Rhineland, Hesse and Franconia, with the southern Netherlands (Austrasia page); Thuringia

ledger.note: 633: Dagobert I gives the Austrasians Sigebert III as sub-king, forced on him by the Austrasian aristocracy. 'Dagobert gave Sigebert III to the Austrasians as a sub-king.' The Austrasia list dates Sigebert III's reign from 634.

region.text: Thuringia under Duke Radulf, who defeated Sigebert III in 640

ledger.note: 640: Duke Radulf of Thuringia rebels and defeats Sigebert III, taking Thuringia out of Austrasia. The Francia page: 'Thuringian duke Radulf rebelled, defeating Sigebert in 640'; the Thuringii page: they 'had regained their independence by the late seventh century under Radulf'.

region.text: Austrasia, when Childeric II is invited to be 'king of the whole realm'

ledger.note: 673: Neustrian and Burgundian magnates invite Childeric II of Austrasia to become king of the whole realm: 'some Neustrian and Burgundian magnates invited Childeric to become king of the whole realm'. Childeric dies in 675.

region.text: Austrasia under Dagobert II, 675-679

ledger.note: 675: After Childeric II's death Theuderic III 'retook his throne' (Francia page) and Dagobert II rules Austrasia (list 675-679).

region.text: Austrasia, received by Theuderic III

ledger.note: 679: Dagobert II dies and Austrasia passes to Theuderic III: 'When Dagobert II died in 679, Theuderic received Austrasia as well.' In 687 Pepin of Herstal after Tertry becomes 'sole mayor and dux et princeps Francorum'; the realm stays undivided until 717.

region.text: the lands between the Meuse, Moselle, Middle Rhine and Main: roughly Luxembourg, eastern Belgium, Lorraine and Champagne-Ardenne, the Rhineland, Hesse and Franconia, with the southern Netherlands (Austrasia page); Alemannia and Thuringia

ledger.note: 741: Charles Martel's sons divide the realm and Carloman takes Austrasia, Alemannia and Thuringia, Pepin Neustria, Provence and Burgundy. The Francia page leaves Aquitaine and Bavaria out of the division.

region.text: Alsace, carved out of southern Austrasia in the last decade of Dagobert I's reign

ledger.note: 742: The Duchy of Alsace is dissolved when no successor to the dead Duke Liutfrid is named; Carloman, ruling Austrasia and Alemannia, suppresses the Alemanni 742-746 (Duchy of Alsace page). The page does not say Alsace passed to Austrasia; that is the reading.

region.text: the lands between the Meuse, Moselle, Middle Rhine and Main: roughly Luxembourg, eastern Belgium, Lorraine and Champagne-Ardenne, the Rhineland, Hesse and Franconia, with the southern Netherlands (Austrasia page); Alemannia, Thuringia and Alsace

ledger.note: 751: The infobox ends Austrasia in 751 (Childeric III, last Merovingian king, 743-751; Pepin III mayor 747-751); the term 'Austrasia' was used only occasionally after the Carolingians took power.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of Thuringia
wars.outcome: Theuderic I and his relatives defeat Herminafrid in two battles and take the Unstrut region; Thuringia is Frankish from 531-532.
wars.note: Gregory of Tours's story of Herminafrid's alliance with Theuderic against his brother Baderich as the page tells it; Burgscheidungen and Chlothar I's part are not on the page.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of the Burgundian kingdom
wars.outcome: 'In 534, Theudebert along with his uncles conquered Burgundy and partitioned it among themselves.' Austrasia's share is not named, so no zone is drawn for Austrasia; the Frankish dossier carries the conquest.

wars.name: Theudebert I's intervention in Italy
wars.outcome: Theudebert invaded northern Italy in 539 but 'his expedition ended soon and retreated due to supply shortages and disease'; he is said to have kept the Alpine passes and, undated, captured the Cottian Alps, parts of Liguria and most of Venetia, which Totila would grant permanently if he won.
wars.note: No lasting gain is recorded by the page, so no zone; the 536 cession of Provence and part of Raetia by Vitiges went to 'the Frankish kings' without a split.

wars.name: Austrasian-Neustrian wars
wars.outcome: 'Neustria and Austrasia fight almost constantly, with Burgundy often mediating' until Chlothar II takes both in 613.
wars.note: No page opened names a contested zone, so none is drawn.

wars.name: Radulf's revolt in Thuringia
wars.outcome: Radulf defeats Sigebert III in 640 and Thuringia leaves Austrasia.

certainty.note: Merovingian partitions are given by cities and rivers, not frontiers; the Rhine, Meuse and Moselle cores are loosely known and the frontiers with the Saxons, Frisians, Alemanni and Bavarians are approximate throughout.

notes: Written for eu-07-x from five Wikipedia pages (Austrasia, Francia, Theudebert I, Treaty of Andelot, Thuringii) plus Chilperic I and Chlothar II (opened for merovingian-neustria, used for the 567, 575 and 599 events) and Duchy of Alsace (opened for duchy-of-alsace, used for the 623, 629 and 742 Alsace events); Battle of Burgscheidungen and Kingdom of Thuringia returned url_not_found. Austrasia is a Merovingian sub-kingdom that Cliopatria does not draw; it sits inside the Kingdom of the Franks shape (kingdom-of-the-franks, eu-07-b), which must subtract this dossier's land in the spans it is alive, or the orchestrator should pick one drawing: 511-554, 561-611, 623-628, 633-672, 675-678, 741-751. The state is hollow in 555-560, 612-622, 629-632, 673-674 and 679-740 (the loss events say where the land went). Not on the pages opened (left undrawn, no memory used): Austrasia's share of the 534 Burgundian conquest and of the 536 Provence cession; Alemannia and Bavaria under Austrasian overlordship; Charibert's 567 share beyond Tours and Poitiers; the Aquitaine cities and Auvergne 'territory' of 575; which cities Austrasia took at Dormelles in 599; Childebert II's 592 inheritance of Burgundy; the 596-613 reach of the Auvergne; the 747 withdrawal of Carloman. A gap-filler should open Gregory of Tours / 'Guntram', 'Sigebert I', 'Childebert II', 'Battle of Tertry' and 'Carloman (mayor of the palace)'. Francia page's 717 sentence ('restricted to Neustria', 'first time since 679 that the kingdom was divided') is ambiguous as summarised; the 717-719 civil war is left to the kingdom-of-the-franks and kingdom-of-neustria dossiers. No infobox area is given, so no area comparison. Wikidata id: not reachable, set to null (the Austrasia article has one). Gazetteer: no region 'Austrasia' or 'Neustria'; the core is a union of modern regions. Names needed: Austrasia, Neustria (regions); Unstrut (river).
